proposal.comment: [Playbook] The indemnity currently runs one way only. We require Licensor to defend us against third-party IP infringement claims relating to the Platform and against claims arising from its breach of law, unauthorised access to our data or wilful misconduct; our own indemnity should stay limited to our content and our breach of law.

ops.text: (iv) Licensor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Licensee and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Licensed Technology or Documentation infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right; (b) Licensor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee's data or client data caused by Licensor; or (d) Licensor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Each indemnified party shall give prompt notice of the claim, permit the indemnifying party to control the defence, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense; no settlement imposing any obligation on the indemnified party shall be made without its consent.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and wilful misconduct.

quote: ARTICLE XII INDEMNITY Licensee will be solely responsible for any commercial or legal liability that may arise as a result of Licensee's exercise of any of the license rights granted by Licensor to Licensee under this Agreement, and Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless from and against any and all suits, claims, proceedings, judgments, awards, damages, loss, liability, cost and expenses
rationale: Article XII is a broad one-way Licensee indemnity (covering even the mere exercise of our licence rights and the conduct of our business) with no Licensor indemnity at all; Article XIII goes further and excludes Licensor from any liability for third-party IP infringement claims arising from the Platform. That is the playbook walk-away. Redline inserts a Licensor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with standard procedure.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We are content that Licensor keeps the Platform, but the Agreement is silent on our own data: we retain all rights in our trading, client and configuration data, and Licensor should hold only a limited processing right. Any customisation work we pay for is licensed to us perpetually and irrevocably.

ops.text: Licensee retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, content, records and configurations submitted to or generated through the Licensed Technology by or on behalf of Licensee or its clients ("Licensee Data"), and Licensor acquires no rights in Licensee Data other than the limited right to process it as necessary to provide the Licensed Technology during the term. No Licensee intellectual property or Licensee Data is assigned to Licensor, and nothing in this Agreement creates joint ownership. To the extent Licensee pays for customisation or development work under Article VII, Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and have modified the resulting work for Licensee's business purposes.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensee ownership sentence for our data and any customer-funded customisations.

quote: ARTICLE III OWNERSHIP Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.
rationale: Licensor's ownership of its own Platform is acceptable, but the Agreement is entirely silent on our data: "Intellectual Property Rights" is defined only as Licensor's rights, and there is no statement that we retain our trading, client and configuration data or any licence back for customisation work we fund under Article VII (which, combined with Article XXI, leaves our data with Licensor). Redline adds a Licensee Data ownership sentence, a no-joint-ownership statement and a perpetual licence to paid-for customisations.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We need a mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000; a one-way cap at half of amounts we have paid leaves us effectively uncapped while Licensor is barely exposed. Indemnification, confidentiality/data-security breaches, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement must sit outside the cap, and our fee obligations are not "damages".

ops.newText: (b) NOTWITHSTANDING PARAGRAPH (A) AND EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY LICENSEE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (II) USD 1,000,000, AND THE EXCLUSION OF DAMAGES IN PARAGRAPH (A) SHALL APPLY EQUALLY TO BOTH PARTIES. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. LICENSEE'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES DUE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT CONSTITUTE DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS CAP.
ops.oldText: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.

proposal.summary: Make the cap mutual, reset the basis to 12 months' fees / USD 1M, and carve out indemnities, confidentiality, IP and wilful misconduct.

quote: (b) IN NO EVENT SHALL LICENSOR'S AGGREGATE CUMULATIVE TOTAL LIABILITY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT EXCEED ONE HALF OF THE AMOUNT PAID BY THE LICENSEE TO Licensor HEREUNDER.
rationale: The cap and the consequential-damages exclusion protect Licensor only, and the cap is one half of amounts we have actually paid — well below 6 months' fees and effectively illusory early in the term. Article II compounds this: we "hereby assume all liabilities and risks associated with the use of the system" and Licensor is excluded from all IP-infringement liability. There are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data/security, indemnities, fraud or IP infringement. This is at the playbook walk-away line; redline makes the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1M with standard Excluded Claims.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We must be able to assign to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets without consent, and a change of control cannot hand Licensor a termination right or a veto based on the identity of our acquirer.

ops.newText: Licensee may assign this Agreement and its license rights hereunder, without Licensor's consent, to an Affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganisation or sale of all or substantially all of its assets; any other assignment by Licensee requires Licensor's prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed.
ops.oldText: Licensee may not assign this Agreement or assign, sublicense and/or transfer in any manner its license rights hereunder in whole or in part without Licensor's prior written consent.

ops.newText: Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall continue in full force and effect, and Licensee shall notify Licensor of such Change of Control within thirty (30) days after its consummation.
ops.oldText: Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor; provided that Licensor will not unreasonably withhold its consent to the consummation of a Change of Control. For purposes of the preceding sentence, Licensor will be deemed to have reasonably withheld its consent to a Change of Control if any person or entity who would acquire direct or indirect control (as defined below) of Licensee pursuant to such Change of Control then conducts a business that is directly or indirectly competitive with a business then conducted by Licensor or any of its Affiliates and/or Licensor reasonably believes that Licensor's interests will be adversely effected by the continuing of this Agreement upon such a Change in Control.

proposal.summary: Permit assignment to Affiliates/successors and delete automatic termination on our change of control.

quote: Upon the occurrence of any Change of Control (as defined below) this Agreement and all Licensee's rights and licenses hereunder shall automatically terminate unless, prior to the occurrence of such Change of Control, Licensor has consented to such Change of Control in a writing executed by an officer of Licensor
rationale: This is our walk-away scenario twice over: a blanket bar on Licensee assignment with no affiliate/M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard (Article XXIV(c)), plus automatic termination on our change of control with a consent veto deemed reasonable whenever the acquirer competes with Licensor. Article XXII also gives Licensor a right of first refusal over a sale of our business, which we should delete separately. Redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out and removes the change-of-control termination trigger.

quote: Licensee acknowledges that the grant of the license set forth in this Section is a non-exclusive license and that the Licensor shall have the right to use and to license to other parties the Licensed Technology for any purpose and in any manner as Licensor may determine in its sole discretion.
rationale: The arrangement is expressly non-exclusive in both directions; there is no sole-supplier, all-requirements or "shall not procure from any third party" obligation on us. The "Right of First Refusal" in Article XXII concerns a sale of our business (addressed under ASSIGN), not procurement exclusivity. No redline required for this rule.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: NO DAMAGES FOR TERMINATION. NEITHER PARTY WILL BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER FOR DAMAGES OF ANY KIND, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties, late-payment interest or minimum termination payment is imposed on us; Article XXIII expressly bars termination damages, and the only cost-shift is the audit cost on a >5% discrepancy, which is within our position. Note there are also no service credits in our favour — worth raising commercially alongside the warranty ask, but no redline needed for this rule.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our Affiliates and the contractors who operate our desk must be covered by the grant, and a licence we pay for cannot be revocable at will — termination should require uncured material breach. We have also added transferability to a successor.

ops.newText: grants to Licensee and its Affiliates and to contractors acting on Licensee's behalf a non-exclusive license, irrevocable during the term except for Licensee's uncured material breach, to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement, and such license is transferable to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Licensee's assets.
ops.oldText: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.

ops.newText: (e) disclose any Licensed Technology to, or permit the use or access of any Licensed Technology by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee, its Affiliates and contractors acting on Licensee's behalf who are bound by confidentiality obligations, for use in the Field of Use.
ops.oldText: (e) disclose any Licensed Technology to, or permit the use or access of any Licensed Technology by any individuals other than the employees of the Licensee for use in the Field of Use.

proposal.summary: Extend the licence to Affiliates and contractors and make it irrevocable during the term absent uncured material breach.

quote: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement
rationale: The grant runs to Licensee alone and Article II(e) limits access to "employees of the Licensee", excluding our Affiliates and the contractors who operate our desk with no path to add them; the licence is also conditioned on payment and terminable by Licensor on any breach, i.e. close to revocable at will, and is non-transferable. Redline extends the grant to Affiliates and contractors, makes it irrevocable during the term absent uncured material breach, and adds successor transferability.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept restrictions on the businesses we operate or the products we buy or build, so we have added a short confirmation that the Field of Use and related restrictions bind only our use of the Licensed Technology. We are content for the restrictions on copying or reverse engineering the Platform to stand.

ops.text: (h) For the avoidance of doubt, the Field of Use limitation and the restrictions in this Article apply solely to Licensee's use of the Licensed Technology and do not restrict Licensee or its Affiliates from operating any business or from developing, acquiring, licensing, procuring or using any other software, platform, service or trading technology, including offerings competitive with the Licensed Technology.

proposal.summary: Confirm the Field of Use restriction limits only use of the Licensed Technology and does not restrain our business.

quote: 1.5 "FIELD OF USE" means, and is limited to, the utilization of the Licensed Technology by the Licensee for the exclusive purpose of fulfilling Spot FX transactions by transmitting market data and orders.
rationale: No express non-compete binds us, but the Field of Use construct plus the Article II restrictions and the change-of-control provision (consent deemed reasonably withheld where our acquirer competes with Licensor) operate as an indirect field-of-use restraint on our business and our M&A options. We accept restrictions on use of the Platform itself, so the minimal fix is a confirmation that nothing restricts us from operating our business or building/procuring alternative FX technology; the competitor-acquirer veto is addressed under ASSIGN.
sectionRef: § I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement:

proposal.comment: [Playbook] In a 36-month term we need a convenience exit on 30 days' notice without penalty, with prepaid fees refunded pro rata; Licensor's immediate termination right should also be limited to uncured material breach.

ops.text: IV Licensee may terminate this Agreement for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Licensor, without penalty or early-termination charge, in which case Licensor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

proposal.summary: Add a Licensee right to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund.

quote: Subject to termination pursuant to this Agreement, the Non Exclusive license granted by Licensor to Licensee shall be for an initial period of 36 months, commencing from the acceptance date, (the "Initial Period").
rationale: There is no Customer termination-for-convenience right in a 36-month committed term, which is our walk-away position, while Licensor may "immediately terminate" on any breach of any covenant with no materiality or cure period. Redline adds a 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; we will also ask that Licensor's termination right be limited to uncured material breach.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Usage audits should be no more than annual, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours and by an auditor bound by confidentiality, with no direct access to our systems. The existing 5% cost-shift threshold is acceptable.

ops.newText: Any such audit shall be conducted no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, during Licensee's normal business hours, on at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice, by an auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations, and without direct or remote access to Licensee's systems; Licensee shall permit such audit within 30 days of its receipt of such notice.
ops.oldText: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.

proposal.summary: Limit audits to once a year on 30 days' notice, during business hours, with no access to our systems.

quote: Any such audit shall be permitted by Licensee within 30 days of Licensee's receipt of a written request of Licensor.
rationale: The audit right has no frequency limit and no notice period (a request can be made at any time, as often as Licensor likes), although the independent-auditor requirement and the 5% cost-shift threshold already match our position. Redline adds once-per-12-months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, confidentiality-bound auditor and no system access.

quote: the parties agree that the validity, interpretation and legal effect of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of New York, U.S.A.
rationale: New York law with exclusive jurisdiction of the federal and state courts in New York City matches our preferred position, and there is no arbitration clause. Note only that Article XXIV(d) adds prevailing-party fee shifting, which is acceptable but we may propose deletion as a commercial point.

quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
rationale: Pricing is a fixed volume-tiered rate card with a 15% rebate and revenue-share ("Supplemental Payments"); there is no obligation on us to extend to Licensor terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, and no matching obligation. Nothing to redline (we may separately seek an MFN in our favour as a commercial ask).
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

quote: The Licensee shall calculate the license fee payable to the Licensor for each month based on the Monthly Notional Volume bands for that pay period and shall pay the Licensor accordingly.
rationale: Fees are purely usage-based against volume bands, with no minimum volume, take-or-pay, shortfall or true-up obligation; the only fixed amounts are the $35,000 initial payment and $2,500/month support fee, which are not minimum purchase commitments. The floor in Article V(III)(b) is measured by actual recorded trades, so it is a reconciliation mechanic rather than a minimum. No redline required.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A three-year, one-way non-solicit covering all Licensor and Affiliate employees is outside our range; we accept only a mutual 12-month restriction limited to personnel directly involved in the engagement. The existing general-advertising carve-out is retained.

ops.newText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the twelve (12) month period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who was directly involved in the performance of this Agreement to leave his or her employment with that party. Neither party is restricted from hiring any person who responds to a general advertisement or who approaches it on an unsolicited basis.
ops.oldText: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.

proposal.summary: Make the non-solicit mutual, cut it to 12 months post-term and limit it to personnel involved in the Agreement.

quote: During the Term of this Agreement and during the three year period after the expiration or termination of this Agreement, the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates to leave his or her employment with Licensor.
rationale: The non-solicit is one-way against us, runs three years post-termination (beyond our 24-month walk-away) and covers all Licensor and Affiliate employees rather than those involved in the engagement. The general-advertising carve-out is fine. Redline makes it mutual, 12 months, limited to personnel directly involved.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A seven-year extension exercisable at Licensor's sole option is not acceptable; renewals should be by mutual agreement for 12 months at a time, with any price increase capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.

ops.newText: The Agreement may be renewed for additional periods of twelve (12) months by mutual written agreement of the parties, and any increase in fees for a renewal period shall not exceed the lesser of the increase in CPI and three percent (3%).
ops.oldText: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.

proposal.summary: Replace Licensor's unilateral 7-year renewal option with mutual 12-month renewals and a capped uplift.

quote: The Agreement may be renewed for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor.
rationale: Renewal is a seven-year extension exercisable unilaterally by Licensor — an automatic multi-year renewal we cannot exit, which is our walk-away position, and there is no cap on renewal pricing. Redline converts this to mutual 12-month renewals with uplift capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
sectionRef: § II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and…

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Article XXI requires us to return everything within five days but says nothing about getting our own trading and client data back. We need up to six months of transition assistance at then-current rates, export of our data in a machine-readable format within 30 days, and certified deletion thereafter.

ops.text: (c) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Licensor shall (i) at Licensee's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Licensor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days, return or export to Licensee all Licensee Data, including trading, client and configuration records, in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete Licensee Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing. Licensee's obligation to return Licensed Technology and Confidential Information shall not require deletion of records Licensee must retain under applicable law or regulation.

proposal.summary: Add transition assistance and return/deletion of our data on termination.

quote: Licensee shall, within five (5) days, ship to Licensor all Licensed Technology, API's Documentation with respect to the Licensed Technology and other Confidential Information in Licensee's possession or control, and an officer of Licensee shall certify in writing that Licensee as complied with the provisions of this Section.
rationale: Article XXI is one-directional: our rights terminate immediately and we must return everything within five days, with no transition assistance, no export of our trading/client data and no deletion certification from Licensor. That is the playbook walk-away for a hosted platform. Redline inserts up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return within 30 days in machine-readable form, and certified deletion, plus a regulatory record-retention carve-out.
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A pure "AS IS" disclaimer with no conformance warranty is our walk-away position for a hosted trading platform. We have added a professional-services warranty and a 90-day conformance-to-Documentation warranty with a repair, re-perform or refund remedy, expressly carved out of the disclaimer.

ops.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing disclaimer, Licensor warrants that (a) the Technical Support Services and any development work will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (b) the Licensed Technology will conform in all material respects to its Documentation during the term; and (c) the Licensed Technology contains no viruses or other malicious code. Licensee's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Licensor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement or, if none is achieved within thirty (30) days of notice, a refund of the fees paid for the affected period. The foregoing warranties are expressly excluded from the disclaimer set out above.

proposal.summary: Add an express performance/conformance warranty with a remedy, carved out of the AS-IS disclaimer.

quote: THE LICENSED TECHNOLOGY IS PROVIDED ON AN "AS IS" BASIS WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND AND LICENSOR HEREBY
rationale: Article VIX is a pure "AS IS" disclaimer that even disclaims that errors or non-conformity to Documentation "CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED", and there is no express performance or conformance warranty anywhere — our stated walk-away for a hosted trading platform. Redline inserts a workmanlike-services warranty, conformance to Documentation, no-malicious-code, and a re-perform/repair/refund remedy carved out of the disclaimer.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Licensor hosts the Platform and handles our trading and client data, so we require standard CGL, tech E&O and cyber cover with certificates on request. This is our standard minimum for data-touching vendors.

ops.text: (l) INSURANCE. Licensor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Licensor hosts or processes Licensee data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Licensor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

proposal.summary: Insert a short insurance covenant in General Provisions.

quote: All payments provided for in this Agreement are exclusive of, (and Licensee shall pay) all taxes, customs, duties, insurance, shipping, and other charges.
rationale: There is no insurance covenant anywhere; the only reference to insurance is a cost we bear. Licensor hosts the Platform and the Hardware and handles our trading and client data, so the absence of E&O and cyber cover is our walk-away. Redline inserts a short insurance paragraph (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, certificates on request) in General Provisions.
